name: Web Brutalism
description: Raw page structure, blunt typography and exposed browser conventions turn a website's construction into its visual identity.

name: Neubrutalism
description: Strong outlines, hard offset shadows and assertive typography make flat interface elements feel deliberately solid and graphic.

sources.title: Neobrutalism components — bold borders and hard shadows

name: Anti-design
description: Clashing scales, awkward alignment and deliberate visual disruption challenge the polished conventions of commercial websites.

sources.title: AIGA Eye on Design — The Era of Rebellious Web Design

name: Net Art
description: The browser, its windows, links and technical behavior become the material of an artwork and the structure of its interface.

sources.title: Rhizome — One Terabyte of Kilobyte Age

name: GeoCities Web
description: Tiled backgrounds, animated graphics and dense personal collections recreate the handmade visual culture of early homepages.

sources.title: Cameron's World — a GeoCities web collage

name: Flash-era Web
description: Choreographed transitions, sound-led sequences and compact animated worlds give navigation the feel of an interactive title sequence.

sources.title: Web Design Museum — historical website gallery

name: Immersive 3D Web
description: A navigable three-dimensional environment organizes the page, making camera position, lighting and spatial scale part of the interface.

sources.title: Codrops — Windland: An Immersive Three.js Experience

name: Holographic Spatial UI
description: Translucent instruments and luminous control surfaces float in depth, forming layered interfaces around a scene or object.

sources.title: Territory Studio — Pacific Rim: Uprising holographic controls

name: Terminal UI
description: Monospaced text, command prompts and a restrained screen palette give the page the direct visual logic of a command line.

name: Text-mode UI
description: Character-drawn borders, text menus and rectangular panels organize information as a complete graphical layout made from type.

name: Classic Macintosh UI
description: Compact bitmap icons, striped title bars and sharply outlined windows establish a crisp monochrome desktop language.

name: Windows 95 UI
description: Beveled gray controls, inset fields and compact title bars make the page resemble a tactile desktop assembled from rectangular modules.

name: Windows XP Luna
description: Rounded window chrome, glossy controls and strongly separated colored title bars bring an approachable consumer-software character to interfaces.

name: Mac OS X Aqua
description: Translucent gel-like controls, polished gradients and softly shaded panels give the desktop the appearance of luminous physical objects.

name: Windows Aero UI
description: Transparent window frames, soft reflections and illuminated controls layer the desktop behind a glass-like interface shell.

name: BeOS UI
description: Short tab-shaped title bars, crisp beveled controls and detailed compact icons create a distinctive modular desktop rhythm.

name: NeXTSTEP UI
description: Dark beveled title bars, square dock tiles and restrained grayscale surfaces give desktop controls a dense workstation character.

name: Amiga Workbench UI
description: Angular bitmap controls, compact iconography and sharply segmented window furniture reflect the visual economy of early multimedia desktops.

name: ANSI Art
description: Colored character blocks and box-drawing symbols form dense illustrations, lettering and menus within a fixed text grid.

sources.title: Sixteen Colors — ANSI and ASCII art archive

name: Teletext Art
description: Large mosaic cells, limited colors and rigid character grids turn screen constraints into bold geometric pictures and text.

sources.title: Dragan Espenschied — teletext and web art

name: Winamp Skinning
description: Custom bitmap panels, miniature instruments and heavily styled controls transform a media-player window into a compact graphic object.

sources.title: Skin Museum — history of Winamp skins

name: CRT Display
description: Scan lines, phosphor glow and visible color cells give digital content the luminous texture of a cathode-ray screen.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

name: Y2K Futurism
description: Chrome surfaces, translucent plastics and streamlined digital forms express the technological optimism surrounding the turn of the millennium.

name: Metalheart
description: Intricate abstract three-dimensional structures, layered technical marks and compressed detail create a dense technological image.

name: Vectorheart
description: Sharp vector forms, industrial symbols and forceful typography create a fast, highly organized version of millennial futurism.

name: Corporate Cyberspace
description: Layered photographs, motion blur and experimental type translate early digital culture into energetic commercial graphics.

name: Gen X Soft Club
description: Muted urban imagery, natural textures and restrained modern type combine a minimal graphic structure with an understated organic mood.

name: Frutiger Aero
description: Glossy interface imagery joins bright skies, water and greenery in an optimistic vision of technology integrated with nature.

name: Acidgrafix
description: Distorted lettering, chrome forms and unusual textures fill compositions with deliberately unstable, densely layered visual energy.

name: Hexatron
description: Angular technology, hexagonal grids and luminous instrumentation create a sharply segmented science-fiction visual language.

name: Cyberbougie
description: Dark surfaces, monospaced details and luminous gradients give technology branding a sleek, computational character.

name: Blob World
description: Elaborate soft-body renders and uncanny textures arrange playful objects into surreal three-dimensional compositions.

name: McBling
description: Rhinestones, metallic shine and conspicuous decorative excess turn early-2000s consumer imagery into a maximal graphic surface.

name: Cyberdelia
description: Fractal forms, kaleidoscopic color and early computer graphics combine electronic technology with psychedelic imagery.

name: Early Cyber
description: Rough pixel imagery, digitally warped lettering and desktop-publishing experiments expose the first wave of computer-generated graphic expression.

name: Silicon Dreams
description: Surreal spaces, primitive geometric objects and conspicuous computer rendering recall the visual imagination of early 3D animation.

name: Laser Grid
description: Perspective grids, glowing lines and reflective surfaces turn 1980s high-technology imagery into a structured futuristic stage.

name: Vaporwave
description: Outdated consumer graphics, early digital imagery and displaced cultural fragments create an uneasy nostalgia for commercial futures.

sources.title: Xiaolong Zhang — What is visual Vaporwave?

name: Webcore
description: Old browser windows, error messages and pixel graphics are remixed into surreal scenes rooted in early internet experience.

name: Weirdcore
description: Familiar low-fidelity images and disorienting text are combined to make ordinary digital spaces feel inexplicably unsettling.

sources.title: Lampoon — Internet aesthetics, Weirdcore and Dreamcore

name: Dreamcore
description: Soft, dreamlike imagery and improbable spaces form a nostalgic visual world that follows emotional association over physical logic.

sources.title: Lampoon — Internet aesthetics, Weirdcore and Dreamcore

name: Cybersigilism
description: Spiked, branching linework fuses symbol-like forms with a digital sensibility, often becoming graphic emblems or ornamental interfaces.

name: Cassette Futurism
description: Bulky controls, angular hardware and analog display cues imagine advanced technology through the physical language of 1970s and 1980s equipment.

name: Fictional User Interface
description: Dense readouts, diagrams and animated instruments give invented technology a coherent visual system for a fictional world.

name: Voxel Art
description: Visible cubic units build objects and scenes, giving three-dimensional imagery the ordered block structure of a pixel grid.

sources.title: Codrops — Turning 3D Models to Voxel Art with Three.js

name: Low-poly Rendering
description: A small number of visible facets simplifies objects into angular silhouettes and broad planes of light.

sources.title: Codrops — Windland: An Immersive Three.js Experience

name: PS1-era 3D
description: Low-resolution textures, unstable polygon edges and coarse shading reproduce the characteristic visual limitations of early console rendering.

name: Cel Shading
description: Discrete bands of light and shadow flatten three-dimensional forms into a graphic image resembling painted animation cels.

name: Wireframe Rendering
description: Visible mesh edges describe form while leaving surfaces open, emphasizing digital construction and geometric structure.

name: Point-cloud Rendering
description: Dense collections of isolated points suggest surfaces and volumes, allowing objects to appear scanned, particulate or partially reconstructed.

name: Gaussian Splatting
description: Overlapping soft volumetric samples reconstruct photographed scenes with an unusually immediate, spatial photographic appearance.

sources.title: Codrops — 3D Glass Portal with Gaussian Splatting

name: Photogrammetry
description: Photographic detail is mapped onto reconstructed three-dimensional forms, retaining surface irregularities and the texture of real objects.

sources.title: Codrops — Blender and photogrammetry case studies

name: Photorealistic 3D
description: Physically based materials and plausible lighting make rendered objects read as photographed surfaces rather than illustrated forms.

name: Chrome Rendering
description: Highly reflective metallic surfaces bend their surroundings into bright highlights and dark contours, emphasizing an object's liquid or sculptural shape.

name: Holographic Graphics
description: Luminous lines, transparent layers and projected volumes make information appear suspended in space rather than printed on a surface.

name: Isometric Rendering
description: Parallel projection presents objects at a consistent angle, creating orderly scenes whose scale remains legible across depth.

name: Anaglyph Graphics
description: Offset color-channel views suggest stereoscopic depth and give edges a deliberately doubled, optically unstable appearance.

name: Matcap Rendering
description: A material-capture texture gives simple geometry a coherent sculptural surface, emphasizing form through stylized highlights and shading.

name: Line-rendered 3D
description: Contours and selected mesh edges replace realistic shading, translating modeled objects into technical or hand-drawn-looking line images.

name: Volumetric Rendering
description: Visible light, fog and semi-transparent density make space itself appear tangible, producing atmospheric depth around objects and type.

name: ASCII Rendering
description: Letters and punctuation replace pixels, describing light and detail through the density of a fixed character grid.

sources.title: Codrops — Efecto: ASCII and Dithering with WebGL

name: Pixel Art
description: Deliberately arranged pixel clusters and limited palettes make each small unit of an image part of its visible construction.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

name: Dithered Rendering
description: Patterns of contrasting pixels simulate intermediate tones, producing a granular surface with a deliberately restricted color range.

sources.title: Maxime Heckel — The Art of Dithering and Retro Shading for the Web

name: Glitch Art
description: Visible failures in digital encoding, display or transmission become the image's structure and material.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman — A Vernacular of File Formats

name: Datamoshing
description: Video-compression structures are disrupted so that movement carries fragments and colors from one frame into another.

sources.title: Carolyn L. Kane — Chroma Glitch: Data as Style

name: Databending
description: Image data is interpreted or altered through unintended processes, producing ruptured colors, bands and unpredictable structures.

sources.title: Rosa Menkman — A Vernacular of File Formats

name: Pixel Sorting
description: Pixels are reordered by visual properties, stretching image areas into organized streaks while retaining traces of the source.

name: Slit-scan Imagery
description: Narrow slices captured at different moments are assembled into one image, stretching movement into continuous ribbons and warped forms.

name: Video Feedback
description: Repeatedly feeding an image back into itself creates recursive tunnels, trails and layered patterns that accumulate over time.

name: VHS Texture
description: Tracking bands, color bleed and unstable tape-like noise give images the worn appearance of analog video playback.

sources.title: Roulette — VX Bliss: Audiovisual Arrangements by Ginny Benson

name: Chromatic Aberration
description: Color channels separate around edges, creating optical fringes that make an image feel refracted, unstable or lens-mediated.

sources.title: V3KTR — optical channel separation and pixel sorting

name: Thermographic Graphics
description: False-color tonal bands replace natural color, turning bodies and objects into vivid fields that resemble heat or scientific imaging.

name: Flow-field Art
description: Many small paths follow a shared directional field, building flowing, hair-like compositions from accumulated motion.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Perlin Noise Flow Field

name: Reaction-diffusion Patterns
description: Simulated chemical interactions generate organic spots and maze-like bands that resemble naturally grown surface markings.

name: Cellular Automata
description: Simple local rules update a grid of cells, creating intricate patterns from repeated small decisions.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Wolfram cellular automata

name: Voronoi Tessellation
description: Space divides into cells around scattered points, producing clustered mosaics with an organic but precise geometric structure.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Weighted Voronoi Stippling

name: Truchet Patterns
description: Repeated tiles rotate and combine into continuous curved paths or networks, creating complexity from a small visual vocabulary.

sources.title: Brad Osgood — Generative art using Truchet tiles

name: Moiré Patterns
description: Overlapping repeated grids or lines create larger interference bands that appear to shift independently of their underlying marks.

name: L-system Graphics
description: Recursively rewritten drawing instructions generate branching structures with the visual rhythm of plants and other growing systems.

name: Fractal Graphics
description: Repeated forms recur at progressively smaller scales, producing intricate images with persistent self-similar structure.

name: Strange-attractor Art
description: Traced trajectories form dense looping structures whose apparent order emerges from a chaotic mathematical system.

name: Particle-field Graphics
description: Large numbers of moving points collectively describe surfaces, currents and shapes that remain visibly particulate.

name: Flocking Graphics
description: Many small agents align, separate and gather into coordinated streams, making collective behavior the primary visual subject.

name: Fluid-simulation Graphics
description: Simulated currents stretch and fold color into swirling plumes, giving digital imagery the behavior of liquid or smoke.

name: Metaball Graphics
description: Soft fields merge into continuous rounded shapes, producing elastic forms that appear to fuse and separate like liquid.

name: Plotter Art
description: Continuous or repeated vector paths create drawings whose precision and accumulated marks reveal a rule-based process.

name: Differential-growth Patterns
description: Curves or surfaces expand at different rates, forming tightly packed folds and organic-looking ridges.

name: Diffusion-limited Aggregation
description: Randomly moving particles gather around a seed to create branching clusters reminiscent of crystals, frost and mineral growth.

name: Lissajous Figures
description: Combined oscillations trace smooth looping curves whose changing ratios produce balanced and intricate geometric forms.

sources.title: The Coding Train — Lissajous Curve Table

name: Topographic Graphics
description: Nested contour lines describe imaginary or real changes in elevation, turning a surface into a flowing diagram of depth.

name: Kinetic Typography
description: Type moves, rotates or changes scale as part of the composition, using timing and rhythm to organize visual attention.

name: Distorted Typography
description: Letterforms stretch, ripple and warp while remaining recognizable, treating text as a flexible visual material.

sources.title: Codrops — Text Distortion Effects using Blotter.js

name: Motion-trail Graphics
description: Repeated afterimages make a moving shape or word leave a visible path, translating time into layered spatial rhythm.

name: Aurora Graphics
description: Soft luminous bands drift across a field, producing a diffuse atmosphere of changing light rather than discrete shapes.

name: Grainy Gradients
description: Fine noise breaks up smooth transitions between colors, giving a luminous digital surface a tactile and atmospheric texture.

sources.title: Codrops — Podium: Grain as a visual language

name: Liquid Distortion
description: Images bend and flow as if seen through moving water, making the surface itself appear unstable and responsive.

name: Particle Typography
description: Many small objects or points assemble into letterforms, so the shape of text remains visible through a particulate structure.

name: Dissolving Typography
description: Letterforms break into dust or fragments, allowing disappearance and dispersal to become part of their visual expression.

sources.title: Codrops — Dissolving Text into Dust and Petals

name: Extruded Typography
description: Visible thickness, perspective and lighting turn letters into sculptural objects that occupy the same space as other three-dimensional forms.

name: Kaleidoscopic Graphics
description: Repeated reflections and radial symmetry transform a small visual fragment into complex rotating fields and ornament.
